scrollPass.cause: window.scrollBy + a SYNCHRONOUS window.scrollY read, breaking on the first moved <= 0. Under html { scroll-behavior: smooth } scrollBy is asynchronous, so the read always saw 0 and the Observer never scrolled the page at all.
fix: window.scrollTo({ top, left: 0, behavior: 'instant' }) — overrides the page's own scroll-behavior
progress measured from a SECOND evaluate taken AFTER the settle wait
SCROLL_NO_PROGRESS_TOLERANCE = 3 consecutive stalls instead of breaking on the first

constants.SCROLL_MAX_STEPS: 40 -> 70 (60 was tried and the suite's own reach inequality caught it: 60 x 0.5 = 30 vh < the pre-28.75 40 x 0.85 = 34 vh)
constants.SCROLL_MAX_TOTAL_MS: 15000 -> 60000 (must not bind before the step cap: 70 x 700 = 49,000)

scrollPass.throughputCost: hobbang.net / went from 28.3s to 120.4s per page (both viewports plus probes). Correctness over throughput, but the closure canary should budget for it.
scrollPass.notMeasured: zeroOpacityNodes / opacityHiddenTextChars on seoultone.kr — those counters are produced by src/responsive-qa/probe.ts (a different lane), and seoultone.kr became unreachable (traffic cap) before it could be re-observed with this fix.
scrollPass.fixtureFadeSplit: Raising the dwell to 700ms also broke two PRE-EXISTING scroll-reveal checks: revealedOpacity is the MAXIMUM opacity sampled, and at 0.5 vh steps a block is on screen for 3 samples (~2,100ms) instead of 2, so any fade the ordering pin admits (< 2,000ms) had already completed and the sampling-floor check went vacuous. The fixture now carries two durations - a CSS transition is taken from the after-change style, so .rv.is-in governs the fade IN (SLOW_FADE_IN_MS 2,600ms) and .rv governs the fade OUT (SLOW_FADE_MS 1,300ms, the ordering pin). A new check asserts the fade-in arithmetic against the fixture's own geometry.
